subject: Physics
prompt: Beyond elastic limit, the material shows?
explain: Beyond elastic limit, permanent (plastic) deformation occurs; material doesn't recover fully.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which point on stress-strain curve represents permanent set?
explain: At yield point, plastic deformation begins; permanent set (residual strain) first appears.

subject: Physics
prompt: Rubber has very small Young's modulus because?
explain: Rubber is highly flexible; it undergoes large deformation for small applied stress → small Y.

subject: Physics
prompt: A ductile material compared to brittle on stress-strain graph shows?
explain: Ductile materials have a large plastic region (e.g., copper); brittle materials fracture just after elastic limit.

subject: Physics
prompt: Brittleness means a material fractures?
options: With little or no plastic deformation
explain: Brittle materials (glass, cast iron) break suddenly with negligible plastic deformation.

subject: Physics
prompt: Resilience is defined as elastic energy stored per unit volume up to?
explain: Modulus of resilience = area under stress-strain curve up to elastic limit; energy stored without permanent set.

subject: Physics
prompt: Toughness of a material is represented by area under stress-strain curve up to?
explain: Toughness = total energy absorbed per unit volume up to fracture; area under entire stress-strain curve.

subject: Physics
prompt: Inter-atomic force is conservative, so elastic restoring force is?
explain: Elastic restoring forces arise from conservative interatomic potentials; energy stored is fully recoverable.

subject: Physics
prompt: Bulk modulus is defined for which states of matter?
explain: All three states resist volume change, so all have a bulk modulus.

subject: Physics
prompt: Compressibility K has SI unit?
explain: Compressibility = 1/Bulk modulus; unit = 1/Pascal = Pa⁻¹.

subject: Physics
prompt: Angle of shear φ (in radians) equals lateral displacement x divided by?
explain: Shear strain = transverse displacement / perpendicular height = x/h.

subject: Physics
prompt: Elastic after-effect refers to?
options: Delay in regaining shape after stress removal
explain: Some materials take time to recover original shape after stress removed — elastic after-effect.

subject: Physics
prompt: Elastic fatigue is the?
options: Loss of elasticity under repeated stress
explain: Repeated cyclic stress causes elastic fatigue — material loses elastic property gradually.

subject: Physics
prompt: If breaking stress of a material is S_b and area is A, breaking force equals?
explain: Breaking force = breaking stress × cross-sectional area.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a rubber band, the stress-strain curve is?
explain: Rubber shows non-linear stress-strain behaviour; it doesn't obey Hooke's law over large range.

subject: Physics
prompt: To increase stiffness of a beam without changing material or length, best option is?
explain: δ ∝ 1/d³; increasing depth d is most effective (cubic dependence) in reducing sag.

subject: Physics
prompt: Stress-strain curve area up to elastic limit gives?
explain: Area under stress-strain curve up to elastic limit = modulus of resilience (energy stored per unit volume).

subject: Physics
prompt: Longitudinal stress is also called?
explain: Stress along the length (axial) of a body is termed tensile (stretching) or compressive (compression).

subject: Physics
prompt: Shear stress is defined as tangential force per?
explain: Shear (tangential) stress = tangential force divided by area over which it acts.

subject: Physics
prompt: Hydraulic stress (volumetric) is the same as?
explain: Uniform pressure from all sides is hydraulic/volumetric stress, SI unit Pa.

subject: Physics
prompt: For an isotropic elastic solid, Y, B, η, σ are related by 3 independent equations; how many are independent constants?
explain: Any isotropic elastic solid is fully described by just 2 independent elastic constants (e.g., Y and σ).

subject: Physics
prompt: Neck formation (localized thinning) in a wire occurs just after?
explain: After UTS, the wire necks (cross-section reduces locally) before fracture.

subject: Physics
prompt: Strain is a dimensionless quantity because it is?
explain: Strain = ΔL/L (or ΔV/V or Δx/L): ratio of same-dimensional quantities → dimensionless.

subject: Physics
prompt: Bulk modulus of water (~2 GPa) compared to air (~0.1 MPa) is?
explain: Water is much harder to compress than air; B_water ≈ 2×10⁴ × B_air.

subject: Physics
prompt: I-shaped girders are used in construction because they have?
explain: I-beam has large effective depth d; since δ ∝ 1/d³, it resists bending efficiently with less material.

subject: Physics
prompt: The property of a material to return slowly to original shape after removing stress is?
explain: Elastic after-effect: time delay in recovery to original shape after stress removed (e.g., glass).

subject: Physics
prompt: The reciprocal of Young's modulus is called?
explain: 1/Y is called compliance or flexibility of the material.

subject: Physics
prompt: Depression at midpoint of a simply supported beam: δ ∝ W·L³/(Y·b·d³). Doubling d gives δ?
explain: δ ∝ 1/d³; doubling depth d reduces depression by factor 8.

subject: Physics
prompt: Interatomic force F vs separation r: at r = r₀, force is?
explain: At equilibrium separation r₀, net interatomic force is zero.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a material, Y = 3B(1−2σ). If σ = 0, then Y/B =?
explain: Y = 3B(1−0) = 3B, so Y/B = 3 when σ = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: The slope of the linear part of F–x graph for a wire gives?
explain: Slope of F–x (force vs elongation) graph = k = YA/L, the spring constant.

subject: Physics
prompt: A material returns to original shape immediately on load removal. This is called?
explain: Immediate and complete recovery of shape after load removal defines perfect elasticity.

subject: Physics
prompt: Area under F–x (force vs extension) graph up to elastic limit equals?
explain: Area under F–x graph = ½Fx = work done = elastic potential energy stored.

subject: Physics
prompt: Poisson's ratio is negative for which type of material (auxetic)?
explain: Auxetic materials expand laterally when stretched; they have negative Poisson's ratio.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a cantilever beam of length L, load W at free end, depression δ ∝?
explain: Depression of a cantilever δ = WL³/3YI, so δ ∝ L³.

subject: Physics
prompt: If n wires of same k are connected in parallel, effective spring constant is?
explain: Parallel combination: k_eff = sum of individual spring constants = nk.

subject: Physics
prompt: Poisson's ratio σ for cork is approximately?
explain: Cork has σ ≈ 0, so no lateral expansion — ideal for bottle stoppers.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a uniform rod rotating about one end, stress is maximum at?
explain: Centrifugal force accumulates from free end; stress is maximum at the fixed end.

subject: Physics
prompt: Modulus of rigidity (η) is defined for which states of matter?
explain: Fluids cannot sustain shear stress, so η is defined only for solids.

subject: Physics
prompt: A wire is stretched. The ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain is?
explain: Poisson's ratio σ is defined as the magnitude of lateral to longitudinal strain ratio.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a wire, if cross-sectional area is halved (same L, Y, F), elongation ΔL?
explain: ΔL ∝ 1/A; halving A doubles ΔL.

subject: Physics
prompt: For which process is bulk modulus of a gas maximum?
explain: B_adiabatic = γP > B_isothermal = P since γ > 1.

subject: Physics
prompt: A steel wire and aluminum wire have same length & force. Which has less elongation?
explain: Y_steel > Y_aluminum, so ΔL_steel < ΔL_aluminum for same F, L, A.

subject: Physics
prompt: The neck/waist formation in wire pulling occurs between which two points?
explain: After UTS, localized thinning (necking) occurs before fracture.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a rubber-like material, the stress–strain curve is?
explain: Rubber is hyperelastic: large non-linear strains but returns to original shape.

subject: Physics
prompt: The restoring force per unit area set up inside a deformed body is called?
explain: Stress = restoring force per unit area; it is the internal reaction to applied deforming force.

subject: Physics
prompt: Practical (engineering) stress is defined as force divided by?
explain: Engineering stress uses original area; true stress uses instantaneous area.

subject: Physics
prompt: In a stress-strain graph for ductile metal, fracture point lies?
explain: After UTS, necking reduces load-bearing area; fracture occurs below UTS on graph.

subject: Physics
prompt: For an isotropic elastic solid, how many independent elastic constants exist?
explain: Y, B, η, σ are related; only 2 are independent (e.g., Y and σ define all others).

subject: Physics
prompt: Hydraulic stress differs from tensile stress in that it acts?
explain: Hydraulic (volumetric) stress is isotropic — equal pressure from all directions.

subject: Physics
prompt: If bulk modulus B is very large for a material, it implies?
explain: Large B means large pressure is needed for tiny volume change — nearly incompressible.

subject: Physics
prompt: The depression δ of a cantilever (length L, load W at free end) varies as?
explain: δ ∝ L³ for a cantilever with point load at free end.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a beam, increasing depth d (keeping b, L, material constant) decreases depression as?
explain: δ = WL³/(4Ybd³), so δ ∝ 1/d³; depth is most effective in reducing sag.

subject: Physics
prompt: For Y = 2η(1+σ) and Y = 3B(1−2σ), eliminating σ gives Y in terms of B and η as?
explain: Standard relation: 9/Y = 3/η + 1/B (or equivalently 9Y = (1/B + 3/η)⁻¹ form).
